items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: And, Mr. Robinson's son, Mundy -- he was the same age I was -- he played drums and I played the fiddle.

ctx.x: record called "WPA" and in later years I found out it was out of print. But I remember I played all that afternoon -- it was all blues, nothing but blues. Big Bill Broonzy. It was all blues dates. I don't know who the other blues guy -- they kept me on it, you know, I was what you might say the house bassist. I think I made $10, which was good money. I made only $10 a week.
But I was in junior high, and every night around 2 o'clock, Mr. Robinson would tell his son, Mundy, he would say, "All right, Mundy, you go on home. Wilbur, you play the rest of the show on drums."

So I had to switch from the bass to drums. I was still playing drums -- always did play drums as well as bass. So I played the rest of the show, and then when I go to school, that's when I started dropping out. I didn't go. I was still working.
